3.name: inspect codicil together
3.description: Asha and the others study the open folder, the journal, and the codicil without touching them, signaling the document's importance.
evidence: The folder lay open on the table between them, the journal's leather edge catching the lamplight and the typed page of the codicil pale beside it, and for a long moment no one moved to touch either.

3.name: Asha verifies signature and witness
3.description: Asha rereads the signature and witness lines, confirming that Rosa signed the codicil as witness.
evidence: Asha read the signature line twice, the shake of the pen unmistakable in the loop of the surname, and then read the witness line, where Rosa's name sat in her own careful hand.

3.name: Lucia's kept page is revealed
3.description: The scene establishes that the codicil page was the one Lucia had been keeping and Rosa had been waiting to discuss.
evidence: It was the page Lucia had been keeping, and it was what Rosa had been waiting to be asked about

3.name: belief question closes
3.description: Asha realizes that the question of whether to believe the codicil has effectively ended between them.
evidence: and between them the question of belief had quietly closed.

3.name: probate challenge looms
3.description: Asha recognizes that the codicil will now have to withstand a legal contest before a probate judge.
evidence: The buyers' hold would lapse in days.
Asha understood, looking at the slight tremor in the typed signature, that any probate judge would see the same thing she did and ask the same questions Daniel was about to learn to ask louder.
The codicil existed. Now it had to survive being contested.

3.name: Daniel stays in doorway
3.description: Daniel remains in the doorway, neither taking the folder nor leaving, showing his hesitation and intent to stay engaged.
evidence: Daniel was still in the doorway, no longer reaching for the folder but no longer leaving the room

3.name: Daniel questions handwriting
3.description: Daniel touches the page carefully and asks why the handwriting changes at the end, beginning his challenge to the codicil's authenticity.
evidence: Daniel finally moved his hand from the chair-back and reached for the page, not snatching it but laying two fingers at its corner the way he might have touched something hot, and asked, in a voice pitched lower than before, why the handwriting looked different at the end than at the beginning.
The question was small and exact, and it told Asha what he had decided to argue: not that the page was forged, but that the woman holding the pen had no longer

3.name: Daniel reframes the codicil dispute
3.description: Daniel argues that the issue is not forgery but that the woman who signed the page may no longer have been the same person.
evidence: he had decided to argue: not that the page was forged, but that the woman holding the pen had no longer been the woman whose name was on it

3.name: Lucia silently challenges Daniel
3.description: Lucia withdraws her hands, fixes Daniel with a steady stare, and silently shifts the room's tension.
evidence: Across the table Lucia drew her palms back from the wood, slow, and let them fall to her sides; she did not speak, but she set her eyes on Daniel and kept them there, and Asha felt the room reorganize around that look

3.name: Rosa brings a brass key to the table
3.description: Rosa enters from the hall and places a heavy brass key beside the codicil, then slides it toward Asha without explaining its lock.
evidence: Behind him there was the soft tread of Rosa coming in from the hall, and Rosa stopped at the table's edge and laid a heavy brass key down on the wood beside the codicil, then slid it the short distance to Asha's hand without a word about which lock it fit

3.name: Daniel falls silent under the key's implication
3.description: Daniel watches the key move across the table and stops speaking, while Asha realizes both sides have now been named.
evidence: Daniel watched the key cross the wood and did not finish the sentence he had begun, and Asha closed her fingers around it and understood that the grounds had now been named on both sides of the table

3.name: Asha returns the key beside the codicil
3.description: Asha turns the key in her hand and slides it back toward Rosa, placing it near the codicil as she takes control of the exchange.
evidence: Asha turned the brass key once between her fingers and then slid it back across the wood toward Rosa, stopping it just short of the codicil so the two objects sat together in the lamplight

3.name: Asha demands what Rosa witnessed
3.description: Asha asks Rosa to describe what she saw Lucia sign, refusing to address Daniel directly.
evidence: "Tell me what you saw her sign," she said, quiet, not looking at Daniel

3.name: Rosa answers with a cryptic warning
3.description: Rosa steps closer, keeps her gaze on Daniel, and replies that a person's mind does not leave all at once.
evidence: Rosa stepped closer to the table and put her hand flat beside the key, her eyes going to Daniel and staying there, and said, "The mind does not leave a person all at once."

3.name: Daniel withdraws into silence
3.description: Daniel pulls his fingers away from the page and refuses to answer Rosa's statement.
evidence: Daniel's fingers, which had been resting at the page's corner, drew back into the half-shadow at his side; he did not answer

3.name: Asha interprets Daniel's silence
3.description: Daniel does not respond to Rosa's statement, and Asha realizes he has heard it as the opening of testimony he must contest by name.
evidence: Daniel's fingers, which had been resting at the page's corner, drew back into the half-shadow at his side; he did not answer
Asha understood that he had heard the sentence as Rosa meant it, as the first line of the testimony he would have to argue against by name

3.name: Asha presents the codicil and key
3.description: Asha slides the codicil and brass key across the table to Rosa and asks her to recount exactly what was signed.
evidence: Asha slid the codicil and the brass key across the wood until they rested in front of Rosa
"Walk me through every word she signed."

3.name: Rosa recounts the signing details
3.description: Rosa declines to pick up the objects and instead describes the kitchen table, the sequence of the signed lines, and the date and witness line.
evidence: Rosa did not pick either object up; she set her fingertips against the edge of the page and began, in a low voice, to describe the kitchen table and the order in which the lines had gone down, naming the date first and the witness line last

3.name: Daniel retreats into shadow
3.description: Daniel steps back from the chair into the shadow by the doorway, avoiding Rosa's eyes as he prepares to challenge the document.
evidence: Daniel stepped back from the chair until his shoulder met the shadow between the lamp and the doorway
from there, not meeting Rosa's eyes

3.name: Daniel questions the missing witnesses
3.description: Daniel asks who witnessed the rest of the document, signaling that he intends to attack the surrounding omissions rather than the signature itself.
evidence: "Who witnessed the rest?"
he would try next—not the signature itself but the pages around it, the absences he could point to in a courtroom

3.name: Asha highlights the missing text
3.description: Asha traces the thin ink and bare stretches on the page, indicating the gaps Daniel plans to exploit, then asks whether anyone else was present.
evidence: Asha leaned over the page and set her fingertip just above the line where the ink had thinned, tracing without touching the small bare stretches Daniel had been counting on
and asked, quiet, "Did anyone else

3.name: Asha questions room entry during silences
3.description: Asha asks whether anyone else entered the room during the periods of silence, probing the integrity of what happened around the codicil.
evidence: asked, quiet, "Did anyone else come into the room during those silences?"

3.name: Rosa reveals she saw everything
3.description: Rosa answers by asserting that she saw the entire sequence of events, refusing to leave Asha's question unanswered.
evidence: "I saw the whole of it," she said.

3.name: Rosa bridges the codicil gap with the key
3.description: Rosa places the brass key across the codicil so it covers the gap between the date and signature, symbolically sealing the absence Daniel relied on.
evidence: she lifted the brass key and laid it across the codicil so its shaft covered the gap between the date and the signature, a flat metal weight bridging what Daniel had wanted to call absence.

3.name: Daniel freezes at Rosa's testimony
3.description: Daniel's hand stops moving at his cuff when Rosa speaks, and Asha realizes his intended argument has been shut down.
evidence: From the shadow at the doorway Daniel's hand, which had been working slowly at the cuff of his sleeve, went still
Asha understood without looking that the line he had meant to draw through the middle of the page had just been closed at both ends in front of him.

3.name: Daniel steps into the lamplight
3.description: Daniel moves out of the doorway shadow into the light and presses Asha with a pointed question about the notary's presence.
evidence: Daniel stepped out of the shadow at the doorway, far enough that the lamplight reached his face again, and asked, "Was the notary present?"

3.name: Daniel adopts a calculated tone
3.description: Daniel speaks in a level, almost helpful voice that suggests a trap rather than genuine cooperation.
evidence: His voice had gone level, almost helpful, the tone of a man laying down a plank he expected someone to fall through.

3.name: Lucia pins the key and page
3.description: Before Asha can answer, Lucia presses her palm over the brass key, holding it and the page down and forcing Daniel to stop.
evidence: Before Asha answered, Lucia leaned in and set her palm flat over the brass key, pinning it and the page beneath it to the wood; she did not look at her brother, but the small flat sound of her hand meeting the metal made him stop where he stood.

3.name: Asha prolongs the silence
3.description: Asha deliberately holds the silence a moment longer so Daniel can hear that he has finally named a group.
evidence: Asha let the silence hold a beat longer than was comfortable, because she wanted Daniel to hear that he had finally named a grou

3.name: Asha silences Daniel's advance
3.description: Asha's hand striking the metal stops Daniel where he stands and establishes her control of the exchange.
evidence: flat sound of her hand meeting the metal made him stop where he stood.
Asha let the silence hold a beat longer than was comfortable

3.name: Asha lets Lucia answer first
3.description: Asha deliberately holds the silence so Daniel hears that Lucia has already answered him before Asha speaks.
evidence: she wanted Daniel to hear that he had finally named a ground, and that Lucia had answered him before she did.

3.name: Daniel retreats and questions the seal
3.description: Daniel steps back from the lamp and asks who verified the notary's seal, trying to keep his tone calm and helpful.
evidence: Daniel took a slow step back from the lamp
"Then who verified the notary's seal?"
The question came out in the same level, helpful tone he had tried before, but it had thinned at the edges.

3.name: Rosa refuses Daniel's framing
3.description: Rosa ignores Daniel's question, fixes him with a direct look, and answers by saying the door was locked.
evidence: Rosa did not answer that question; instead she looked straight at Daniel
and said, "The door was locked."
The three short words landed before the notary one had finished settling

3.name: Rosa redirects the argument to the room
3.description: By refusing to answer the seal question, Rosa forces Daniel back to the physical facts of the room, the table, and the closed door.
evidence: Rosa was not going to follow him onto the ground he had chosen—that she was going to keep returning him to the room itself, the table, the closed door, the people who had been inside it.

3.name: Daniel loses his next question
3.description: Daniel fidgets with his cuff and abandons the follow-up question he had been preparing.
evidence: Daniel's hand went back to his cuff, working at nothing, and he did not ask the next question he had clearly been preparing.

3.name: Asha reclaims the codicil and key
3.description: Asha pulls the codicil and brass key toward herself, moving them out of the lamp-lit center and placing them by her elbow.
evidence: Asha drew the codicil and the brass key across the wood toward herself
a slow deliberate slide that took both out of the lamp-lit center of the table and set them at her own elbow

3.name: Asha confronts Daniel directly
3.description: Asha lifts her eyes and holds Daniel's gaze, asserting herself as the next speaker.
evidence: and then she lifted her eyes to Daniel and held them there.

3.name: Daniel hesitates under Asha's stare
3.description: Daniel initially does not move, his fingers still working at his cuff as Asha holds his gaze.
evidence: He did not move at first; only the small working of his fingers at his cuff stoppe

3.name: Asha sets documents beside herself
3.description: Asha places the papers at her own elbow and fixes Daniel with a steady stare.
evidence: set them at her own elbow, and then she lifted her eyes to Daniel and held them there.

3.name: Daniel hesitates and looks away
3.description: Daniel stops fidgeting, exhales sharply, and looks toward the hallway before speaking again.
evidence: He did not move at first; only the small working of his fingers at his cuff stopped, and his breath went out of him in a short, audible push
He looked away from all three of them, toward the dim shape of the hallway

3.name: Daniel asks for the original log
3.description: Daniel abandons his earlier line of questioning and asks where the original log is.
evidence: "Where is the original log?" he asked
he had abandoned the notary and the seal and was reaching now for something further off

3.name: Asha shields the codicil
3.description: Asha pulls the codicil closer to her body, signaling that she is withholding something from Daniel.
evidence: Asha drew the codicil another inch closer, tucking it almost against her ribs

3.name: Asha challenges Daniel's assumption
3.description: Asha quietly asks Daniel why he thinks she did not bring the original log, forcing him to lean in to hear her.
evidence: "Why do you think I didn't bring it?" she asked, soft enough that he had to lean a little to catch it

3.name: Daniel withholds a response
3.description: Daniel does not answer Asha and resumes his nervous cuff-fidgeting.
evidence: He didn't answer; his fingers found his cuff again and stopped there, halfway to a gesture he didn't complete.

3.name: Rosa backs Asha with the journal
3.description: Rosa taps the journal and states that its entries do not lie while keeping her gaze on Daniel.
evidence: From the other side of the table Rosa reached out and tapped the cover of the journal at Asha's elbow, twice
"The entries don't lie," without taking her eyes off Daniel.

3.name: Daniel realizes the log is missing
3.description: Daniel looks at the journal and understands that the logbook he hoped was upstairs is no longer there.
evidence: He looked at the journal then for the first time, and Asha watched him understand that whatever he had been hoping was still upstairs in a logbook had already bee

3.name: Daniel realizes the journal is the missing evidence
3.description: Daniel looks at the journal and understands that what he hoped was still upstairs has already been brought into the room in their mother's handwriting.
evidence: He looked at the journal then for the first time, and Asha watched him understand that whatever he had been hoping was still upstairs in a logbook had already been carried down into this room, in writing, in their mother's hand.

3.name: Asha opens the journal to the final entry
3.description: Asha turns the journal back to the last entry their mother made, aligning it with the date on the codicil.
evidence: Asha drew the journal flat in front of her and turned its pages back, slow and deliberate, until she found the last entry their mother had made
the same date the brass key still pinned to the line of the codicil at her elbow

3.name: Rosa confirms the date match
3.description: Rosa does not need to inspect the page because she already knows the significance of the matching dates.
evidence: Rosa did not lean over to look; she already knew.

3.name: Rosa orders Daniel to read the dates
3.description: Rosa presses a finger on the journal and tells Daniel to read the dates while staring him down.
evidence: Instead she set one finger square on the cloth cover, just at the corner of the open page, and said, "Read the dates," without lifting her eyes from Daniel's face.

3.name: Daniel compares the handwritten and typed dates
3.description: Daniel reads the dates and realizes the mother's handwritten entry and the typed page were created within hours of each other in the same house.
evidence: Daniel looked, because at that point there was nowhere else in the room to put his attention

Asha watched the small movement at his jaw as he matched the day in their mother's handwriting to the day on the typed page and understood that the two documents had been made within hours of each other, in the same house, by a woman who had still been keeping her daily account.

3.name: Daniel falls silent and braces himself
3.description: Daniel says nothing and places his hand on the table for support as the implication sinks in.
evidence: He did not speak; his hand left his cuff and settled, finally, flat on the edge of the table, as if he needed something solid to stand against.

3.name: Asha slides the journal under Daniel's hand
3.description: Asha moves the open journal so the final entry lies directly beneath Daniel's palm, forcing him to confront it physically.
evidence: Asha eased the journal across the table until its open edge slid beneath Daniel's flattened hand, so that the last entry in their mother's thin late ink lay directly under his palm.

3.name: asha slides journal to daniel
3.description: Asha moves their mother's journal across the table until its open page sits under Daniel's hand.
evidence: Asha eased the journal across the table until its open edge slid beneath Daniel's flattened hand

3.name: daniel feels the final entry
3.description: Daniel keeps his hand on the page, testing the writing beneath it and reacting physically to the discovery.
evidence: so that the last entry in their mother's thin late ink lay directly under his palm
He did not lift his hand at once; he held it there a moment as if testing what was beneath it
Asha watched the knuckles whiten faintly before he drew back, slow, the way a man pulls away from something hot

3.name: daniel withdraws from the page
3.description: Daniel slowly pulls his hand away from the journal after sensing the significance of what is written there.
evidence: he drew back, slow, the way a man pulls away from something hot

3.name: daniel avoids asha's gaze
3.description: After withdrawing, Daniel looks at his own hand instead of meeting Asha's eyes, showing discomfort or hesitation.
evidence: When his hand was off the page he looked at it instead of at her

3.name: daniel asks who witnessed signature
3.description: Daniel asks who saw the final signature, shifting the scene into a more pointed legal inquiry.
evidence: he said, without quite finding her eyes, "Who witnessed the final signature?"

3.name: rosa withholds an answer
3.description: Rosa stays silent instead of answering Daniel's question, forcing the moment to linger.
evidence: Rosa, on the far side of the lamp, did not answer; she only let the silence sit long enough that Daniel had to hear himself having asked
